translations.title: Sick Autumn
translations.text:
Sick and beloved autumn,
you will die when the hurricane blows through the rose gardens,
when snow falls
upon the orchards.

Poor autumn,
you die amid the whiteness and abundance
of snow and ripe fruit.
Deep in the sky
hawks fly
over simple water sprites with short green hair
who have never loved.

At the distant borders
the deer bellow.

And how I love, O season, your sounds,
the fruit that falls and no one gathers,
the wind and forest weeping
all their tears in autumn, leaf by leaf.

The leaves
trampled.
A train
passing.
Life
slips away.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: O Time, O Singular Path from One Point to Another
translations.text:
O time, O singular path from one point to another,
if I were allowed to act, I would quickly change
the hearts of men, and everywhere
there would be only beautiful things.

Instead of defeated brows and instead of penances,
instead of despair and prayers,
there would be everywhere
reliquaries, chalices, and monstrances
shining deep in dreams like those
primitive deities whose poetic function
is almost over.

If I were allowed to act, I would buy
the captive birds to set them free;
I would watch with unstained joy
as they took flight, knowing nothing
of a virtue called recognition,
unless it were gratitude.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: I Write Alone by the Shifting Light
translations.text:
I write alone by the shifting light
cast by a burning log.
Sometimes shells lament,
and often

I hear the gallop of a horse crossing
the distant field.
The owl's sinister cry
rises to heaven; my hand

traces these lines in desolation.
Farewell, my heart.
I also trace, mystically,
the sign of the Great Illusion.

O my mystical love, O Lou, life
will give us the double fire
of delight that never dies.
Later we shall share

a love that will be the only love.
Farewell, my heart.
A mystical star kindles its fire.
It has the color

of the ambiguous color of your gaze
that burns among the shadows.
I feel a sharp wound reopen.
Farewell. It is late.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: A Bird Sings Somewhere, I Know Not Where
translations.text:
A bird sings somewhere, I know not where;
it must be your soul, ever watchful,
hiding among the soldiers.
Its song enchants and wakes me.

Listen, it sings so tenderly.
I do not know which branch it sings from,
but night and day, forever,
weekday and Sunday, it enchants me.

What to say of the loving bird,
its miraculous transformation,
of the soul singing on the branch,
of love into heaven and heaven into rose?

The soldier's bird is love,
and my love is a beautiful girl.
The rose is less lovely, and for
me alone the blue bird trills.

Bird blue as the heart,
blue that weeps within my chest,
let me hear your sweet song
above the deadly machine gun

that crackles in the distance.
Do they sow stars with their song?
So goes the night, so goes the day;
blue love, blue as my heart.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Here You Are Beside Me Again
translations.text:
Here you are beside me again,
memories of my comrades killed in the war,
the olive of time,
memories that are only one memory,
like a hundred skins making only one cloak,
like those thousands of wounds that are only a newspaper item.

Impalpable and shadowy presence that has seized
the changing shape of my shadow,
an Indian lying in wait through eternity,
shadow, you drag yourself beside me,
but you no longer hear me;
you will no longer know the lovely poems I sing,
while I still hear you, still see you.

Fate,
multiple shadow, may the sun keep you,
you who love me enough never to leave me,
who dance in sunlight without raising dust,
shadow, ink of the sun,
writing of my life,
coffer of sorrows,
a god who humbles himself.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Bestiary or Procession of Orpheus
translations.text:
I. The Dromedary

With four dromedaries,
Don Pedro of Alfarubeira
went through the world and admired it.
He did what I would do
with four dromedaries.

2. The Tibetan Goat

The hair of this goat, and those
golden fleeces that enchanted
Jason, are nothing beside
the locks that have made me fall in love.

3. The Locust

This is the slender locust,
the food of Saint John;
may my verses, like it,
be bread for good people.

4. The Dolphin

Dolphins, you play in the sea,
but the waves are bitter.
Does joy sometimes well up in me?
Life is always merciless.

5. The Crab

Uncertainty, we shall go far
and happily, never to return,
as crabs do,
backward... backward...

6. The Carp

In ponds and pools,
how long you live, O carp!
Has death perhaps forgotten you,
fish of melancholy?

translations.title: The Bonfire
translations.text:
I threw into the noble fire
that I carry and adore
living hands and fire itself,
that Past, those heads of the dead.
Flame, I do what you wish.

That sudden gallop of stars,
being no more than what it will become,
mixes with the male neighing
of centaurs in their breeding places
and with the great vegetable laments.

Where are those heads I once had?
Where is the God of my youth?
Love has turned bad.
May the flames be reborn in the bonfire.
My soul undresses in the sun.

Flames have grown across the plain.
Our hearts hang from the lemon trees.
The severed heads that acclaim me
and the stars that have bled
are only women's heads.

The river pinned over the city
fastens you there like a garment.
Setting out from the docile amphion,
you suffer all the enchanting tones
that make the stones nimble.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To Lou...
translations.text:
Four days without a letter from you, my love.
The day no longer exists; the sun has gone out.
The barracks have become a house of terror,
and I am as sad as an escort horse.

What has happened to you? Are you suffering, darling? Do you weep?
You promised you would always write to me.
Send your letter, a shell from your artillery,
to bring me back to life and make me smile.

Eight times now the mail corporal has answered me,
“No letter for you,” and I have almost cried.
I search the neighborhood for that lovely lost dog
we once saw together, O beloved heart.

Thinking of you, I pet him for a long time.
I think he remembers the day we saw him,
for he licks me and looks at me tenderly,
and he is the only friend I know in Nîmes.

Without news of you I feel desperate.
What are you doing? I wish for a letter tomorrow.
The day has darkened until it turns golden,
and sadly, my Lou, I kiss your hand.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Mirabeau Bridge
translations.text:
Mirabeau Bridge watches the Seine flow by,
watches our loves flow by,
and reminds the peaceful soul
that joy always follows sorrow.

Night comes, the hour sounds,
and the days drift away
and leave me here.

Let us face each other, our hands entwined,
while beneath the bridge
of our arms pass, weary,
the silent depths of our two gazes.

Night comes, the hour sounds,
and the days drift away
and leave me here.

Love escapes us like this running water;
love goes from us,
life goes slowly by.
How powerful is newborn hope.

Night comes, the hour sounds,
and the days drift away
and leave me here.

The slow day and peaceful night flee,
but never return
the times gone by, nor love, nor sorrow.
Mirabeau Bridge watches the Seine flow by.

Night comes, the hour sounds,
and the days drift away
and leave me here.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
